text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَٰرُونَ وَفِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ ۖ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ سَٰبِقِينَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that carries the prior list forward
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a real continuation, carrying the named figures into the destruction inventory from 29:38. Its attached shape also starts the clipped triadic beat, so the boundary feels syntactically porous rather than like a fresh story opening.

topics.headline: opening cross-boundary continuation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first connector makes this ayah depend syntactically on the previous destroyed-object chain.
topics.reason: The rows point to coordination, prior governance, and a boundary-crossing object chain.

topics.headline: attached particle starts the triadic beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the list begin with a compact repeated connector before each name.
topics.reason: The form and cadence rows describe the attached one-letter connector and repeated list rhythm.

words.gloss_range: definite foreign proper name in the carried accusative object chain, concentrating the Qārūn wealth figure into one named item
words.prose: {{ar:قَارُونَ}} ({{tr:qārūna}}) is a governed proper name, not a generic wealth label. The accusative diptote form makes the famous wealth figure grammatically acted upon, while his first position compresses the longer wealth narrative of 28:76-82 into one culpability marker and lets economic power open the wider power taxonomy also echoed by the three-name grouping at 40:24.

topics.headline: governed proper name, not generic wealth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Qārūn is a specific named object in the carried verdict, not a generic symbol floating outside the syntax.
topics.reason: The QAC and noun-instance evidence support accusative diptote proper-name status in the carried object chain.

topics.headline: wealth power compressed into one name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees economic power compressed into a single named figure before political power is named.
topics.reason: The semantic rows preserve Qārūn as the wealth profile while grammar keeps him acted upon.

topics.headline: first slot in the power triad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the longer Qārūn wealth narrative in 28:76-82 is compressed into one first-slot name inside a broader power triad also attested at 40:24.
topics.reason: The intertext and structure rows identify the rare three-name grouping and the first-slot role.

words.gloss_range: medial connector coordinating the second name as a peer inside the same carried case frame
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the second name inside the same coordinated case frame. The reader hears another short hinge between heavy names, making royal power a coordinate peer of wealth rather than an apposition or restart.

topics.headline: second connector equalizes the next name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second name is coordinated as a peer under the same case frame, not made an explanation of the first.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence supports coordination inside the same carried sequence.

topics.headline: attached medial hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the list as equal pulses because the small connector recurs before the next heavy name.
topics.reason: The form and sound rows describe the fused connector and clipped audible hinge.

words.gloss_range: definite foreign title-name in accusative coordination, invoking the known political tyrant without making him the clause subject
words.prose: {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) enters as the known title-name of political tyranny, but the accusative diptote form keeps him inside the object chain. His central position matters: royal power is flanked by wealth and administration rather than monopolizing the scene, and the large Moses-Pharaoh narrative load is compressed into one coordinated slot.

topics.headline: famous ruler as governed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Pharaoh is grammatically demoted into the same object chain despite his royal title.
topics.reason: The proper-name and diptote rows match the accusative coordinated noun evidence.

topics.headline: political tyranny in the center
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees political dominion named at the center of a wider power array rather than as the only antagonist.
topics.reason: The semantic rows connect the title-name to political tyranny while preserving proper-name reading.

topics.headline: Moses confrontation compressed into one slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes that a frequent Moses-Pharaoh confrontation field is compressed into one middle triad member.
topics.reason: The occurrence, co-occurrence, and structure rows support compression, central placement, and the Moses-proof confrontation frame.

words.gloss_range: final list connector that admits the third name as a coordinate peer and completes the triad
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the third name while closing the enumeration. The repeated connector gives the list its designed third pulse, so administrative complicity is not an afterthought but a coordinated member of the same verdict frame.

topics.headline: third connector completes the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the third figure is coordinate and completive, not an appended afterthought.
topics.reason: The rows describe coordination plus closure of the three-item list.

topics.headline: final list pulse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the enumeration finish as a balanced third pulse before the emphatic report begins.
topics.reason: The form and cadence rows preserve the attached connector and audible completion.

words.gloss_range: definite foreign proper name in the same accusative chain, making the administrative enabler a named accountable member of the triad
words.prose: {{ar:هَامَانَ}} ({{tr:hāmāna}}) is a specific proper name in the same governed chain. His usual dependence on Pharaoh in 28:6, 28:8, 28:38, 40:24, and 40:36 becomes locally visible as a coordinate slot, completing the wealth, rule, and administration sequence before the proof-bearing clause begins.

topics.headline: specific administrative figure governed with the others
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Hāmān is a named accountable object in the same case chain, not just Pharaoh’s background aide.
topics.reason: The noun evidence supports proper-name diptote form and coordination.

topics.headline: administration added to the power system
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the opposition become institutional, with administrative machinery named beside wealth and rule.
topics.reason: The semantic rows treat Hāmān as administrative enablement inside the triad.

topics.headline: subordinate pairing expanded into a full triad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a name paired with Pharaoh in 28:6, 28:8, 28:38, 40:24, and 40:36 is given its own coordinate slot and helps complete the system-wide taxonomy.
topics.reason: The intertext and structure rows support Hāmān’s repeated Pharaoh pairing, rare occurrence profile, and triad culmination.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector shifting from the named list into the certified Moses report
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from the accused list into a certified report. Because it is attached to the la-qad frame, transition and assertion arrive together: the ayah remains connected to the inventory while opening the Moses evidence scene.

topics.headline: resumptive shift into the evidence clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah pivot from listing accused powers to certifying the proof event that explains their guilt.
topics.reason: The clause evidence and CRITICAL rows support a resumptive transition into the main Moses report.

topics.headline: connector fused to the emphasis package
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees transition and certification compressed into one surface cluster.
topics.reason: The form row describes the connector attached to the la-qad assertion package.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle within the la-qad assertion frame, strengthening the completed arrival report
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is not a lexical item to translate by itself; it is the emphatic first part of the la-qad package. Moses' arrival with evidence is asserted first with force, before the ayah narrates the arrogant response.

topics.headline: emphatic lām over the arrival report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof-bearing arrival is asserted with force before the response is narrated.
topics.reason: The translation-support evidence and rows identify the emphatic lām plus qad frame.

topics.headline: bound prefix before the response beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees emphasis built into the clause opening before the arrogance clause can appear.
topics.reason: The form and structure rows show the bound lām placed before the perfect arrival clause.

words.gloss_range: certification particle before a perfect verb, marking the arrival as realized and established
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) certifies the following perfect arrival as realized. Its scope stays on that completed proof-event, so the later arrogance is judged as a response to established evidence rather than as a separately certified achievement.

topics.headline: certified completed arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that certainty attaches to Moses’ completed arrival with proofs, not to the later arrogance itself.
topics.reason: The rows and translation support identify qad before a perfect verb as certification with local scope.

topics.headline: independent preverbal particle in la-qad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the assertion unfold in two particles before the response hinge.
topics.reason: The form and structure rows preserve the visible particle sequence.

words.gloss_range: completed arrival to specified recipients with proofs borne in a bi-phrase; delivery force survives, while causative clarification is not the selected local verb
words.root_gloss_range: broad arrival and coming field, including reaching and bringing; the local perfect verb with object suffix and bi-phrase selects arrival-to-recipients with delivered proof-content
words.prose: {{ar:جَاءَ}} ({{tr:jāʾa}}) is the first finite verb after the triad, turning the noun list into an evidentiary scene. The attached plural object makes the named powers the recipients reached, while the bi-phrase makes the proofs something brought into their presence; the proof-arrival thread also links this scene with 29:31 and 29:33. The root {{ar:ج ي أ}} ({{tr:j-y-ʾ}}) supports arrival and delivery here, but the Form I verb leaves causative making-clear to the proof noun rather than selecting that as the verb's own form. Its hamza gives the arrival verb a sharp audible catch before the flowing object suffix gathers the recipients.

topics.headline: arrival reaches named recipients with proofs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a full confrontation frame: the named powers are reached, Moses is agent, and proofs are carried into the scene.
topics.reason: The verb frame has an object suffix and a bi-prepositional complement, with Moses as subject.

topics.headline: Form I arrival, not causative clarification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb frames completed arrival and delivery, while the proof noun carries the clarification force.
topics.reason: The local Form I frame licenses coming/reaching with delivery force, but not a causative making-clear verb.

topics.headline: proof arrival linked to 29:31 and 29:33
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this arrival as part of a local messenger-arrival pattern, with 29:31 and 29:33 as comparanda.
topics.reason: The intertext and structure rows connect the verb to proof delivery, local arrivals at 29:31 and 29:33, and the boundary shift.

topics.headline: audible catch at the arrival verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a sharp catch at the proof-arrival verb before the recipients are gathered by the suffix.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a distinct sound payoff tied to the local verb.

words.gloss_range: definite proper name functioning as the post-verbal agent of the arrival, not as proof-content itself
words.prose: {{ar:مُوسَى}} ({{tr:mūsā}}) follows the verb as the explicit agent. That placement keeps Moses as the one who comes bearing proofs, while the single prophet stands against the three-name opposition panel and joins the recurring Moses-with-clear-proofs formula cited at 7:103, 11:96, and 40:23-24.

topics.headline: post-verbal Moses as agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Moses is the arriving agent and bearer of proofs, not the proofs’ grammatical substitute.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies Moses as the subject of the arrival verb.

topics.headline: one prophet against the power panel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a structural asymmetry: one proof-bearing prophet stands against a three-name power complex and an established proof formula visible at 7:103, 11:96, and 40:23-24.
topics.reason: The rows connect Moses with Pharaoh, clear proofs, proof scenes at 7:103, 11:96, and 40:23-24, and the contrast with the evidence mode in 29:38.

words.gloss_range: preposition attaching the proof noun to the arrival verb as accompaniment and operative means
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the arrival verb to the proof noun. It leaves accompaniment and instrument both live: Moses comes with proofs, and those proofs are the operative means by which the confrontation reaches the triad. As a compact liaison, the particle makes that dependency visible and audible before the proof noun is processed.

topics.headline: proofs as accompaniment and instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proofs are both what Moses comes with and the means by which the confrontation operates.
topics.reason: The local prepositional complement attaches the proof noun to the arrival verb.

topics.headline: small particle visibly and audibly binds the proof noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears the proof phrase as bound to the arrival, not as a free-standing noun.
topics.reason: The form and liaison rows preserve the fused dependency.

words.gloss_range: definite plural clear proofs governed by bi-, with the root field of separation and clarification narrowed to evidentiary distinction
words.root_gloss_range: broad field of separation, interval, relation, appearance, disclosure, and clarity; the local noun selects clear proof while retaining distinction as the active image
words.prose: {{ar:الْبَيِّنَاتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}) closes the certified mission clause on evidence rather than on Moses alone. As a definite plural, it presents recognized, multiple clear proofs; the root {{ar:ب ي ن}} ({{tr:b-y-n}}) narrows to proof while retaining the image of distinction that separates truth from ambiguity. The same clarity field links 29:35, 29:38, and 29:49, while this noun makes clarity delivered and portable in the confrontation. Its doubled central yāʾ gives the evidence word extra sound weight, and its placement directly before the response particle makes the arrogance a refusal after clarity has arrived.

topics.headline: recognized plural proofs as carried content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause ends on a governed, definite, plural proof category rather than on vague indication.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under bi, definite, plural, and attached to the arrival frame.

topics.headline: proof narrowed from the distinction root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that proof here is not bare persuasion; it carries the root image of clarity that separates truth from ambiguity.
topics.reason: The broad b-y-n field includes separation and clarity, but the local noun selects clear proofs.

topics.headline: clear-proof network across the surah and corpus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees clarity move from visible ruins to delivered proofs and onward to later clear signs, with 29:35, 29:38, and 29:49 in view.
topics.reason: The rows connect the noun with same-surah clarity at 29:35, 29:38, and 29:49, proof delivery, and the immediate response pivot.

topics.headline: sound weight at the proof noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears extra weight at the word that names the evidence.
topics.reason: The sound row supplies a distinct local cadence payoff.

words.gloss_range: consequential response particle that turns clear proof into the immediate scene of arrogant refusal
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the quick hinge from evidence to response. It marks immediate consequence and ironic reversal at once: clear proofs should lead to submission, yet the next clause makes arrogance the narrated result. Coming after the long proof noun, the clipped particle makes the turn into arrogance feel abrupt.

topics.headline: proof turns immediately into response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the moral sequence: established proofs first, then arrogance as the immediate narrated response.
topics.reason: The clause evidence marks the arrogance clause as a result after the Moses report.

topics.headline: short fused turn after the long proof noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the abruptness of the turn from clear proofs into arrogance.
topics.reason: The form and sound rows preserve the attached short response particle.

words.gloss_range: Form X plural perfect selecting self-claimed greatness as a collective completed response, extended by the following land-domain phrase
words.root_gloss_range: broad greatness field including size, rank, age, majesty, hardship, and self-magnification; local Form X narrows it to arrogant self-estimation after evidence
words.prose: {{ar:اسْتَكْبَرُوا}} ({{tr:istakbarū}}) gathers the three named figures into one plural actor and narrates their response as completed. The Form X shape from {{ar:ك ب ر}} ({{tr:k-b-r}}) turns neutral greatness into self-claimed greatness, and the following land phrase makes that self-inflation public and territorial rather than private pride. The same root later contrasts with what is truly greater in 29:45, while the territorial stage recalls wrongdoing in the land at 29:36. Its s-t-k-b-r cluster gives the self-magnifying verb a dense sound before the long plural ending.

topics.headline: plural arrogance after proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the three named figures become one collective actor in a completed response after evidence.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect plural with pro-drop subject continuity and a following land-domain complement.

topics.headline: self-claimed greatness from the greatness root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the precise moral shift: neutral greatness language becomes self-estimation against received proofs.
topics.reason: The broad k-b-r field is narrowed by Form X to arrogant self-magnification rather than all greatness branches.

topics.headline: self-inflation made territorial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees arrogance as a public land-domain formula, with 29:36 and 29:45 sharpening the same-surah contrast.
topics.reason: The rows connect k-b-r with land, proof rejection, same-surah contrasts at 29:36 and 29:45, and arrogance-in-land parallels at 7:36, 46:20, and 40:56.

topics.headline: dense sound of self-magnification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the arrogance verb as weightier than the surrounding hinges.
topics.reason: The sound row gives a local acoustic payoff for the consonant cluster and plural ending.

words.gloss_range: locative/domain preposition that moves arrogance from inner posture into the land-sphere
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) is the small hinge that gives arrogance a domain. It does not make land the direct object; it locates and spreads the self-magnifying posture within the public sphere of power.

topics.headline: arrogance located in a land-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the arrogance is not merely inward; it is placed in a spatial and political domain.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the land noun and attaches to the arrogance verb.

topics.headline: separate small bridge to the land noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees an explicit bridge from the arrogance verb to the domain phrase.
topics.reason: The form rows describe the free preposition as a compact but separate domain marker.

words.gloss_range: definite singular land-domain governed by fī, allowing both known political territory and broader earth-domain without making land the acted-upon object
words.root_gloss_range: broad concrete field of ground, land, earth, and territory; local governance by fī selects domain or arena for public arrogance
words.prose: {{ar:الْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) completes the arrogance scene as a governed domain phrase. The root {{ar:أ ر ض}} ({{tr:ʾ-r-ḍ}}) can name ground, land, earth, or territory; here the Pharaoh-Moses setting specializes it toward political territory while the broader earth-domain keeps the arrogance-in-land wording general. The land phrase also ties wrongdoing, arrogance, and consequence across 29:36, 29:40, and 29:52, and its hamza onset gives the response clause an audible landing point.

topics.headline: land as governed arena, not direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that land is the arena of arrogance, not the thing directly acted upon.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after fī and functions as the prepositional complement of the arrogance verb.

topics.headline: territory and earth-domain both live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scale tension: Pharaoh’s political territory is local, while the earth-domain wording generalizes the arrogance.
topics.reason: The arḍ field allows ground, land, earth, and territory; local context specializes without collapsing the range.

topics.headline: land-domain parallels at named references
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the land phrase link wrongdoing, arrogance, and consequence across 29:36, 29:40, and 29:52.
topics.reason: The rows connect the land noun to arrogance-in-land parallels at 7:36, 46:20, and 40:56 and to the same-surah earth-domain sequence at 29:36, 29:40, and 29:52.

topics.headline: audible landing at the domain noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the domain noun as the landing point of the response clause.
topics.reason: The sound row supplies a distinct payoff for the word’s onset in context.

words.gloss_range: connector before negation that links the final verdict to the arrogance clause with coordinate and concessive force
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the verdict turn without detaching it from the arrogance clause. It can coordinate the final statement and also make it concessive: though they filled the land with self-importance, the next words deny any capacity to get ahead. Because it is bound to the negation opening, the verdict begins as a joined transition rather than a detached maxim.

topics.headline: connector turns from arrogance to negated verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verdict remains bound to the arrogance clause while undercutting it concessively.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks the final clause as a contrast linked to the arrogance clause.

topics.headline: connector fused to the negation opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verdict begin as a bound transition into negation.
topics.reason: The form row describes the connector joined to the following negation.

words.gloss_range: negation particle scoping over the copular predicate, denying a state of outstripping rather than one isolated attempt
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) gives the negation its own visible slot before the copula. Its scope covers the state named by the final predicate, so the ayah denies being outstrippers, not merely a single failed escape attempt. The long open vowels at the start of the closure slow the verdict after the clipped response hinge.

topics.headline: negation scopes over the copular predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial targets a state of being outstrippers, not merely one attempted escape.
topics.reason: The translation support explicitly says the negation scopes over the kāna predicate.

topics.headline: standalone negation before the copula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears negation occupy its own slot at the start of the verdict beat.
topics.reason: The form and cadence rows preserve the standalone particle and long-vowel opening.

words.gloss_range: negated copular perfect with plural subject continuity, assigning the final participle as a denied state or identity
words.root_gloss_range: broad being and occurrence field, with place and status extensions; local defective verb under negation selects predicated state rather than formation, command, or simple action
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا}} ({{tr:kānū}}) carries the final clause toward its predicate and keeps the same plural group in view. Under negation, the root {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) works through copular being: the verdict says they never occupied the state of outstrippers, and the adjacent endings in 29:38 and 29:39 make the reversal from insight-capacity to escape-incapacity structural. Its long vowel pairs with the final predicate to slow the closing cadence after the dense arrogance verb.

topics.headline: denied state assigned to the plural group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict denies what the triad ever were, not just what they failed to do.
topics.reason: The verb instance is copular and the final participle is its predicate.

topics.headline: being-root narrowed to predicated status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices existential force in the verdict while keeping it within the local copular construction.
topics.reason: The k-w-n field supports being and status, but local defective kāna blocks formation or command branches.

topics.headline: 29:38-29:39 closure reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 29:38 and 29:39 as adjacent closure frames: insight is affirmed, escape-capacity is denied.
topics.reason: The rows identify the adjacent endings at 29:38 and 29:39 and the being-plus-outstripping pairing.

topics.headline: long-vowel final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verdict slow into its closing predicate.
topics.reason: The cadence row gives a distinct payoff for the long vowels in the closing phrase.

words.gloss_range: indefinite masculine plural active participle as predicate of the negated copula, denying durable membership in the class of outstrippers or escapers
words.root_gloss_range: broad field of preceding, racing ahead, outstripping, stakes, and escape; local active participle under negation selects denied status as those able to get ahead of consequence
words.prose: {{ar:سَابِقِينَ}} ({{tr:sābiqīna}}) is the final landing word. As an indefinite active participle under negation, it denies durable membership in the class of those who get ahead; the root {{ar:س ب ق}} ({{tr:s-b-q}}) keeps the race and escape image concrete. That makes the close answer the same-surah outstripping question at 29:4 and prepares the consequence catalogue in 29:40: these named powers were not outstrippers in any relevant sense. The long -īna ending lets the denial land on an extended final sound.

topics.headline: active participle predicate denies durable class membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word denies an identity or capacity, not one completed act of outrunning.
topics.reason: The noun is an indefinite active participle and the predicate of the negated copula.

topics.headline: race and escape image in the final denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the concrete motion image: the powers cannot outrun, preempt, or get ahead of the verdict.
topics.reason: The s-b-q field supports preceding, racing, and outstripping; local negation narrows it to denied escape-capacity.

topics.headline: answer to the earlier outstripping question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing word answer 29:4 and set up the consequences listed in the next ayah.
topics.reason: The rows connect the final predicate to 29:4, precedence contexts at 36:40, 23:61, and 21:27, closure position, and next-ayah consequence.

topics.headline: extended final sound seals the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the denial land on an extended final ending.
topics.reason: The sound row gives a distinct closure payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence in which Moses comes with clear signs, the rulers make themselves great, and they are denied any outstripping.
baseline_models.mechanism: The signs are actively brought into the rulers' presence and disclose what is at issue; their self-exaltation follows that exposure, while the closing pursuit image denies that territorial command can become escape.

activation_trace.role: Bringing or presenting something makes Moses' coming an active placement of the signs before the named rulers.
Visible disclosure makes the signs an exposure against which the following self-exaltation reacts.
Arrogant self-greatness supplies the resistant response to what has been made clear.
Getting away from a pursuer gives the final negation a pursuit-and-non-escape contour.

changed_reading.before: Moses came with clear proofs; the rulers acted arrogantly and did not escape.
changed_reading.after: Moses makes disclosure present before them; their self-enlargement is a response to that exposure, but it cannot convert control into escape from what follows.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coupling of self-greatness in the earth with the denial of forward precedence.
baseline_models.mechanism: Images of magnitude, the lower plane, adhesion to the ground, and forward racing create a two-axis irony: apparent vertical enlargement occurs on low ground and yields no horizontal lead.

activation_trace.role: Magnitude opposed to smallness gives the self-exalting form a spatial image of claimed size.
The lower plane opposite the sky locates their claimed magnitude within a bounded low domain.
Adhesion and heaviness toward the ground provide a material analogy for power that cannot lift free.
Forward movement in a race supplies the denied horizontal lead.

changed_reading.before: They were arrogant in the land and unable to get away.
changed_reading.after: Their power is pictured as inflation on the lower plane: apparent height without forward lead, and territorial largeness that remains earthbound.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier question about wrongdoers supposing they can outstrip, followed by the denial of evasive power in earth or sky, turns the focus ending into the answer to a recurring escape calculation.

activation_trace.role: Escape from a pursuer anchors the focus clause as the terminal denial in a repeated race motif.
Supposition or estimation makes attempted outstripping a mistaken calculation rather than a demonstrated capacity.
The same escape-from-pursuit image states explicitly what evildoers imagine they can achieve.
Evading pursuit or making the pursuer fail turns spatial incapacity into a direct counterpart of non-outstripping.
The earthly domain grounds one half of the verse's exhaustive denial of an exit in earth or sky.

structural_cues: 29:4 places the outstripping verb inside a rhetorical question about an evildoer's supposition.
29:22 coordinates inability in the earth with inability in the sky, closing both spatial exits.
29:39 repeats the outstripping root under explicit negation after earth-bound self-exaltation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated outstripping wording, the supposition frame, and the earth-or-sky inability frame; I infer a race against divine seizure or accounting, while the live alternative is the narrower idiom that they simply could not escape.

changed_reading.before: The rulers happened not to get away after rejecting Moses.
changed_reading.after: Their non-escape instantiates the surah's recurring diagnosis of a bad calculation: wrongdoing never gains a usable lead or an outside jurisdiction.

context_deltas.mechanism: A clear sign is left after one destroyed community, another outcome is visible from its dwellings, and then Moses brings clear signs before the focus rulers; warning evidence and aftermath evidence form one cycle in which refusers can become evidence for later viewers.

activation_trace.role: Presentation makes the focus signs the pre-refusal phase of the proposed evidentiary cycle.
Visible disclosure anchors the signs as evidence already clear before the rulers exalt themselves.
A manifest marker supplies the surviving evidentiary object left after the preceding destruction.
Visible disclosure characterizes the remnant as clear aftermath evidence.
Becoming visibly clear from former dwellings extends disclosure from a delivered sign to an inspectable outcome.

structural_cues: 29:35 says that a clear sign was left from the destroyed settlement.
29:38 locates what became clear in the former dwellings of prior peoples.
29:39 places signs before arrogance, and 29:40 immediately places seizure after it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a sign left after destruction, clarity from dwellings, and signs delivered before the focus refusal; I infer that refusal converts its agents into later evidence, while the live alternative is that these are independent examples with no designed evidence cycle.

changed_reading.before: The clear signs are only Moses' warning proofs addressed to the three rulers.
changed_reading.after: They are the first phase of a two-sided disclosure: evidence arrives before refusal, and the refusers' outcome can remain as evidence afterward.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding exemplar links embellished deeds to diversion from an extended path while insight remains; this makes the focus response to clear signs readable as motivated redirection of perception rather than simple lack of perception.

activation_trace.role: Visible disclosure anchors the focus problem in acknowledged clarity rather than unavailable evidence.
Arrogant self-greatness supplies the focus mechanism that can redirect a perceiver after disclosure.
Making conduct appear good supplies the altered valuation that precedes diversion.
Turning away or diverting converts embellished valuation into blocked movement.
An extended traversable path gives the diversion a directional target.
Insight of the heart preserves perceptual capacity even while that capacity is redirected.

structural_cues: 29:38 orders adornment, diversion from the path, and retained insight in one sentence.
29:39 follows directly with clear signs and then a response introduced by immediate sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the adjacent sequence of adornment, diversion, path, and insight; I carry that mechanism into the focus sequence as motivated resistance, while the live alternative is that verse 38 describes only the prior peoples and does not diagnose the three rulers.

changed_reading.before: The rulers reject clear signs because pride leaves them unable to see.
changed_reading.after: The text permits sight to remain active: embellished practice and self-ranking redirect discernment away from the disclosed path, so arrogance is obstruction despite insight.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next verse answers earth-bound self-exaltation and non-outstripping with universal seizure by offense and differentiated capture, including sinking through earth and drowning; the rulers' apparent domain becomes one of the media that enclose them.

activation_trace.role: The earthly lower domain begins as the field in which the rulers display their claimed greatness.
Failure to escape pursuit anticipates the concrete capture mechanisms listed next.
Offense or culpability supplies the stated attachment between each seizure and its agent's deed.
Ground sinking converts earth from a field of dominance into an active capture medium.
The repeated earth image makes the spatial reversal explicit across the verse boundary.
Drowning adds water as another enclosing medium through which attempted escape ends.

structural_cues: 29:40 immediately opens with an all-inclusive seizure formula tied to each one's offense.
29:40 repeats a distributive some-of-them construction across distinct modes of capture.
The focus places self-exaltation in earth immediately before earth itself participates in one capture.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate adjacency, universal seizure, and differentiated earth and water captures; I infer a reversal from territory to enclosure, while the live alternative is a simple punishment catalogue, and the packet does not assign each mode to a particular named figure.

changed_reading.before: They exercised arrogant power on earth but eventually failed to flee.
changed_reading.after: Earth is not neutral territory beneath their power: the next verse turns created media into capture mechanisms, exposing territorial mastery as enclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later use of the same greatness root for divine remembrance supplies a rival scale: the focus rulers assign greatness to themselves within earth, while the later formulation relocates what is greater.

activation_trace.role: Self-ascribed grandeur anchors the focus as a claim to improperly held greatness.
Magnitude opposed to smallness gives the later statement about divine remembrance the scale that corrects the focus claim.

structural_cues: 29:39 uses a self-exalting form of the greatness root inside the earth.
29:45 uses the same root in the statement that remembrance of God is greater.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the uncommon same-root echo and two different bearers of greatness; I infer a scalar correction of the rulers' self-measurement, while the live alternative is that the two uses are semantically independent.

changed_reading.before: They became arrogant after Moses showed them proofs.
changed_reading.after: They misassign magnitude within the earth; the later same-root statement supplies a competing scale that exposes self-greatness as a measurement error.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus arrival of signs is followed later by the possible arrival of punishment at a fixed term and without warning; non-outstripping bridges the two arrivals, so the interval after disclosure is delay within a limit rather than a successful lead.

activation_trace.role: Bringing something into presence establishes the signs as the first arrival in the sequence.
Failure to get away from pursuit links the first arrival to an unavoidable later endpoint.
A fixed temporal limit supplies the boundary within which apparent delay operates.
Coming or occurring makes punishment the second arrival that closes the interval opened after warning.
Sudden surprise removes the practical value of any apparent temporal lead.

structural_cues: 29:53 conditions delayed punishment on a named term and then emphatically says it will arrive suddenly.
The focus orders arrival of signs before the denial that the rulers can get ahead.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an arrival of signs, a denied lead, and a later arrival governed by a fixed term and surprise; I infer a two-arrival warning structure, while the live alternative is that 29:53 addresses a later audience without glossing the ancient rulers.

changed_reading.before: The rulers could not outrun the consequences of rejecting Moses.
changed_reading.after: The signs' arrival opens a bounded interval whose second arrival is fixed and potentially sudden; waiting after warning never becomes a temporal lead.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the tail-or-end branch of the offense root where culpability is the primary sense. It remains valid as a material analogy tied to the focus pursuit image and the next verse's seizure, but downstream prose must not present tail as the verse's translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The denial that the rulers can get away from pursuit.

activation_trace.role: Escape from a pursuer supplies the runner whose attempted lead must eventually close.
Culpable offense preserves the primary causal link between deed and seizure.
A trailing end or tail supplies the exploratory image of consequence remaining attached behind the runner.

changed_reading.before: Each is seized for his offense because none can escape.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the offense is also the trailing end that catches the would-be runner: consequence remains attached behind them until pursuit closes.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a rare nominal water-gathering branch far from the ordinary verbal sense of coming. It remains anchored in the focus arrival root and is activated by the immediate drowning image, but downstream prose must label it a material analogy, not a lexical translation or historical claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Moses' coming with signs followed by the rulers' failure to escape.

activation_trace.role: Water collecting in a depression or around a defense supplies a remote image of arrival becoming gradual enclosure.
Actual presentation of the signs keeps the remote water image attached to the focus act of bringing evidence.
Drowning in water activates the enclosure potential of the focus root's distant water branch.

changed_reading.before: Moses came to powerful rulers with proofs, but they could not escape.
changed_reading.after: As a deliberately remote material analogy, the coming of the proofs resembles water gathering around a defended enclosure until no route remains.

strongest_changes: The focus denial of outstripping becomes the answer to a surah-wide mistaken escape calculation rather than an isolated closing phrase.
Clear signs become a two-phase evidence system: disclosure before refusal and visible residue after judgment.
Earth reverses from the rulers' field of self-enlargement into one of the media of capture.
The arrival of signs and the term-bound sudden arrival of punishment make delay a bounded interval, not a lead.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah order makes 29:39 a hinge: visible remains precede it, differentiated seizure follows it, and later root echoes recalibrate greatness and arrival. Its compact sequence therefore joins evidence, space, scale, and time rather than merely listing defeated rulers.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not map the distinct punishments in 29:40 to individual names, so the capture model remains distributive rather than biographical.
The greatness echo in 29:45 may be a deliberate scalar correction or an independent reuse of the root.
The evidence-cycle reading depends on treating adjacent exemplars as a designed sequence; they can also be read as separate cases.
Both outliers are branch-driven analogies and should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Self-magnification mistaken for outstripping.** ك ب ر B006 is grandeur and self-magnification, and B011 is contending and overcoming. Their response to clear proofs is to enlarge themselves “in the earth,” but the closing race term denies that they got ahead. I infer that spatial dominance is treated as temporal escape; arrogance reads as an attempted expansion beyond accountability that fails to outstrip it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The spider-house in 29:41 supplies a surprising structural judgment on earthly grandeur: self-enlargement can rest on the weakest support. Failure to outstrip is thus architectural as well as temporal.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Self-magnification is a failed vertical strategy inside the earth.** Lexical evidence: `ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا`, root `ك ب ر`, `B006` (grandeur and self-magnification); `ٱلْأَرْض`, root `ء ر ض`, `B001` (lower ground opposite sky); and `سَابِقِين`, root `س ب ق`, `B004` (outstripping or escaping another). Structural cue: they magnify themselves “in the lower ground,” yet cannot get ahead; `29:40` immediately gives earth-sinking and drowning, while `29:44` attributes the whole sky-earth frame to divine creation. Assigned role: self-magnification attempts elevation; the earth locative contains it; failed precedence cancels escape. Abductive move: the vertical irony is inferred from branch images, not explicitly stated. Reading change: arrogance becomes an attempted but impossible spatial elevation within a field they do not control.

2. **Clear disclosures make the failure one of rank-protection, not missing evidence.** Lexical evidence: `جَاءَهُم`, root `ج ي ء`, `B004` (bringing or presenting something), and `ٱلْبَيِّنَات`, root `ب ي ن`, `B005` (disclosing meaning by expression or sign). Structural cue: presented clarities precede self-magnification by `فَ`; `29:38` likewise combined evidence and insight with diversion. Assigned role: disclosure supplies sufficient epistemic access; magnification supplies the countervailing social posture. Abductive move: I infer that the signs threaten claimed rank and are resisted for that reason; the packet establishes sequence, while the motive remains abductive. Reading change: their rejection reads as defensive self-elevation in the face of clarity.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later confirmation (`29:44`):** Creation of the entire sky-earth frame with firm truth closes the spatial irony of self-magnification “in the earth.” Their attempted elevation and escape occur inside a proportioned structure whose scale, integrity, and ownership are not theirs.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyüklük ve ululuk yanında insanın kendini üstün görmesiyle ortaya çıkan böbürlenmeyi açıkça destekler. Geçici çerçevenin Tanrı'ya özgü hak edilmiş ululuk yönü ayrı söz birimi kanıtında bulunur, fakat yetkili dal iddiasında açıkça kurulmadığı için dal tanımının çekirdeğine alınmamıştır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, ululuk ve kendini üstün görme alanındadır; özel inançsal niteleme yalnız ilgili söz biriminin karşılığında korunur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın ululuk ve üstünlük taslama alanını verir; başka dallardaki büyüklük, yaş veya başkanlık anlamlarını içeri almaz.

facets.statement: Ululuk, üstünlük ve başkalarından yukarıda olma düşüncesi anlamın temel eksenidir.
İnsanda bu eksen, kendini beğenme, başkalarından üstün sayma ve büyüklük taslama biçiminde gerçekleşir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ululuk ve büyüklük anlamında birleşir; insan davranışında bunun kendini beğenme, üstün sayma ve büyüklük taslama biçimini aldığını belirtir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi soy yakınlığındaki önceliği ve en büyük çocuğu aktarırken, aynı aile içi söz öbeği için bazı aktarımlar son doğanı, bir başkası en büyük olanı bildirir. Dal soy ve doğum sırasındaki konumu ortak çatı olarak koruyabilir, ancak tek ve uzlaştırılmış bir sıra değeri ileri süremez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Soydaki yakınlık ile doğum sırası aynı alan içindedir; son doğan ve en büyük çocuk aktarımları kaynak varyantları olarak ayrı tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Soy bakımından öncelik bildiren biçim ile aile içi doğum sırasını bildiren kalıp ayrılır; çelişen sıra değerleri birleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin soy zincirindeki yakınlık veya aile içindeki doğum sırası bakımından belirli bir konum taşımasıdır; aktarımlar ilgili aile söz öbeğini kimi yerde son doğan, kimi yerde en büyük çocuk olarak açıklar.

facets.statement: Soy zincirinde daha yakın ve öncelikli konumda bulunma anlam alanının bir bölümüdür.
Aile içi söz öbeği bazı aktarımlarda son doğan çocuğu, başka bir aktarımda en büyük çocuğu bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu iddia soy yakınlığı ve doğum sırasını aynı alanda toplar; aile içi sıra için kaynaklar son doğan ile en büyük çocuk arasında uzlaşmayan iki değer aktarır.
